title: VERIFY cluster 3 (the formal records): replay publish/show/cite, and audit each record against the addendum text it claims to enact
description: Verdict T-358, the epic's flagship act. Two failure modes matter here and neither is caught by running the test suite: a record that cites a DIRECTIVE and then says something weaker or wider than the DIRECTIVE says, and a record that looks like an overruling but is actually a restatement. Replay the transcript, then read the addendum section each record cites and put the two texts side by side. Rotation slot 3: your identity must have produced no artifact in this epic, must not be `verifier-final`, and must differ from the identities executing T-359, T-360 and T-362.
acceptance_criteria: REPLAY EVERY PUBLISH COMMAND from T-358's handoff transcript IN A TEMP ROOT (`--root <tmp>`), never against the live registry, and confirm each produces a structurally identical record. A command that cannot be re-run as quoted is a REJECT: the transcript is the evidence, and an unreproducible transcript is not evidence. Report any command that had to be repaired to run.
FOR EVERY MINTED RECORD IN THE LIVE REGISTRY: `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-NNN` and `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite PR-NNN`, each exit 0, output pasted in your verdict.

TEXT-AGAINST-SOURCE AUDIT - the check nothing else in this epic performs. For each record, open docs/serenissima-addendum-legal-theory.md at the section its `sources` cite and confirm the record's ratio actually ENACTS that section rather than paraphrasing it into something weaker, wider or merely adjacent. Quote the addendum sentence and the record's ratio SIDE BY SIDE in your verdict. A record that cites a DIRECTIVE and states something else is a REJECT, not a wording note.

THE A2 RECORD SPECIFICALLY: confirm it is an OVERRULING act and not a restatement. Its target anchor must RESOLVE when you run the CLI (paste the command and output). Its reasoning must be present and must include the PRESERVED half of T-344's argument - that any N>1 threshold would be a de facto ban on binding, that authority_tier remains issuance authority, that a single verdicted decision still binds, and that what changes is the ceiling, not the floor. Confirm the record does NOT claim to change authority_tier semantics. Its operation type must match A4's taxonomy and you must say which type and why it is right.
SELF-CONFIRMATION CHECK: every minted record has confirmation_status unconfirmed and confirmed_by null (SDR-02). A producer-confirmed record is an automatic REJECT.

NO HAND-EDITS - prove it, do not assume it: for every minted id, find the corresponding precedent_published event in .harness/logs/events.jsonl (paste the grep), and confirm the record file's field order and defaults match a CLI-minted record rather than a hand-authored one. A record with no publish event is a REJECT.

LEDGER COMPLETENESS: check T-358's record ledger against the ledger fixed in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-v1-requirements.md. Every addendum section 2 through 7 is either covered by a record or explicitly accounted for. A silently skipped DIRECTIVE section is a REJECT.

SOURCE TOKEN FORM: confirm every record's sources carry the DOI token 10.22201/iij.24487937e.2026.20.20316 plus section in the exact form the synthesis fixed, and that NO record cites the addendum by a docs/ path (gitignored, .gitignore:33 - it would dangle for every clone). Run `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite --all` and `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts` against the live registry, paste exit codes and complete findings, and account for every finding - the baseline is the single known PR-001 P-023 dangling token.
`python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v` still green with your own 'Ran N tests' line quoted (P-025).

VERDICT T-358 via `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py update T-358 --status done --agent <you> --note "..."` or `--status open` with a REJECTED: note. RECORD YOUR REVIEWER IDENTITY and confirm in writing that you are not `verifier-final`, produced no artifact in this epic, and are not the identity that executed T-359 or T-360.

--- PR-005, sources doi:...#2 + T-352, addendum section 2 DIRECTIVE ---
ADDENDUM: "Any precedent-layer schema MUST separate: 1. Identification/
determination of the ratio ... 2. (Re)interpretation of the ratio -- what
that norm means; includes declarative interpretation (fixing an indeterminate
ratio for a new case) and corrective interpretation (arguing the previously
identified ratio was merely apparent and the real ratio differs; includes
restrictive and extensive corrections). 3. Valuation of the ratio --
ascribing its institutional force ... This is metatextual: it changes force,
not meaning." + "A single 'precedent' blob conflating these three makes
disagreement unadjudicable. Schema fields, conflict detection, and the
overruling protocol must know which of the three operations a session is
performing."
RATIO: "Every interpretive act recorded in the registry is typed as exactly
one of three operations, structurally separate: `determination` (the
publish-time recorded choice ... since the interpreter chooses rather than
merely recognizes a pre-existing meaning), `reinterpretation` (`declarative`
when it fixes an indeterminate ratio for a new case, `corrective-restrictive`
or `corrective-extensive` when it argues the originally identified ratio was
merely apparent and states a narrower or wider real ratio), and `valuation`
(a metatextual act that changes a ratio's institutional force ... without
touching its meaning) ... Conflict detection and the overruling protocol
branch on this typing: a record may never carry an untyped 'precedent' blob
conflating identification, reinterpretation, and valuation, because doing so
makes disagreement about which of the three happened unadjudicable."
FINDING: ENACTS. Three-way separation, both correction directions, the
metatextual/force-not-meaning discriminator, and the branching duty all
carried. It also adopts the realist reading the section's own terminological
caution directs. The one clause with no addendum antecedent -- the default
`{"type":"determination","subtype":null}` when a publish supplies none -- is
V1-13's, which labels default-to-determination "planner judgment" while
anchoring the field's PRESENCE to A4; T-352 is a cited source, so the clause
is sourced, and it cannot weaken the DIRECTIVE because the field is still
always present and always typed.

--- PR-006, sources doi:...#3 + T-352, addendum section 3 DIRECTIVE ---
ADDENDUM: "The successor retains the corrective path: it may argue the
declared ratio is apparent/incorrect -- but ONLY by reinterpreting the source
materials that produced the decision, with recorded reasoning, at sufficient
authority level. Correction without sources is mere disagreement and is
invalid." + "Therefore every precedent record MUST carry a sources field ...
Second-degree documents without their first-degree sources make founded
overruling impossible."
RATIO: "a successor retains a corrective path: it may argue a declared ratio
is merely apparent and state the real one, ONLY by reinterpreting the source
materials that actually produced the original decision, with recorded
reasoning, at an authority tier no lower than the original. Because a
second-degree document (a precedent) without its first-degree sources makes
founded overruling impossible, every registry record -- of any tier, of any
operation type -- MUST carry a non-empty `sources` field ... A corrective
reinterpretation, or an overruling/voiding act, that cites no sources is
mechanically REFUSED at publish (exit 1): correction without sources is mere
disagreement."
FINDING: ENACTS. "at an authority tier no lower than the original" is a
CONCRETIZATION of "at sufficient authority level", not a substitution: it is
the shipped tier-symmetry rule (SDR-17.8, refuse when the acting tier NUMBER
exceeds the target's), so the record states the mechanical form of the
DIRECTIVE's open term rather than a different rule. Scope of the sources
mandate is if anything wider in the DIRECTIVE's own direction ("of any tier,
of any operation type"), matching V1-11. See also the cleared reading noted
under SOURCE-PRECISION-A on "bind at publication".

--- PR-008, sources doi:...#4 + T-352, addendum section 4 DIRECTIVE ---
ADDENDUM: "Serenissima SHALL maintain the interpretive code as an explicit,
versioned system artifact, identical for all sessions" + "Every interpretive
act cites the code version used." + "two sessions that disagree either read
different dispositions, used different code versions, or applied the same
code differently -- three distinguishable failure modes instead of one fog."
+ "The code itself is amendable only through the overruling-grade protocol
(it is constitutional-tier material)."
RATIO: "Serenissima maintains the interpretive code ... as an explicit,
versioned system artifact identical for all sessions, not composed ad hoc and
privately by each interpreter ... Every interpretive act recorded in the
registry cites the code version it applied (`interpretive_code_version`), so
that when two sessions disagree, the disagreement decomposes into one of
three distinguishable failure modes -- a different disposition read, a
different code version cited, or the same code version applied differently --
instead of one undifferentiated fog. The code is constitutional-tier
material: amendable only through the overruling-grade protocol, at tier 1 or
2, naming the rules changed and the version bump; an ordinary edit to the
document without a published amending record is invalid."
FINDING: ENACTS. See INTERPRETIVE-CODE-A for the one clause examined and
cleared ("at tier 1 or 2" against A3's parenthetical "tier-2 path").

--- PR-009, sources doi:...#5 + T-352 + T-344, addendum section 5 via A2 ---
ADDENDUM: "Reiteration raises force (jurisprudencia constante; also observed
de facto in common law via accumulating citations -- Llewellyn): a ratio's
force level increases with N consistent applications across sessions,
recorded via the citation index. A never-recited ratio may decay to
persuasive." + "Force is graded, not binary."
RATIO: "Reiteration is a first-class force-raising mechanism at every tier,
computed on read from the citation index (addendum section 5: jurisprudencia
constante; Llewellyn's accumulating citations): a tier 1-3 record with three
or more qualifying consistent applications (the C counter) computes force
`settled`, above plain `binding`; a tier-4 record with three or more computes
force `reiterated`, above plain `persuasive`. A never-recited ratio may decay
to persuasive (flagged only, never auto-expired)."
FINDING: ENACTS, and the concretizations are all sourced: N=3 is R-2's own
disclosed threshold with its bracket (carried, not invented), the graded enum
is V1-22's, "flagged only, never auto-expired" is the addendum's own section
6 logic as A2 directs. The overruling half is audited in full in the T-358
verdict note (section 6) and is not repeated here.

RATIO: "Force is a value computed on read, never a stored field on any

count of strictly-later-published records in the same root, never wall-clock

FINDING: ENACTS. Every quantitative claim checks out against the synthesis

--- PR-011, sources doi:...#6 + T-352, addendum section 6 DIRECTIVE ---
ADDENDUM: "precedent records MUST carry validity conditions (what facts about

RATIO: "Every registry record at tiers 1-3 must carry a non-empty

--- PR-012, sources doi:...#7 + T-352, addendum section 7 (NOT DIRECTIVE) ---
ADDENDUM: "Intentions of collective bodies ... are not discoverable facts;
appeals to them are normative moves, not descriptions. Do not build

RATIO: "No mechanism in this registry may presuppose recoverable collective

... Anti-evasion design must therefore constrain fact re-description itself,

difference is material ... Legal/institutional certainty is not a property a

interpretive process."
FINDING: ENACTS all three bullets, with A6's (a)/(b) structure made explicit.

=== OPEN-QUESTIONS (upstream, routed to T-362) ===

OPEN-QUESTION: DIRECTIVE-A -- PR-011's ratio is narrower than the section 6
DIRECTIVE it enacts. The addendum says "precedent records MUST carry validity
conditions", unqualified; the record says "Every registry record at tiers 1-3
must carry a non-empty `validity_conditions` field". Tier-4 records are
thereby exempt from a DIRECTIVE that exempts nobody. NOT chargeable to T-358:
the narrowing is T-352's, stated in its own field table at V1-10 row 28
("required non-empty tiers 1-3; optional (default []) tier 4 ... tier
parallel to #10 is planner judgment mirroring SDR table #10's own tier
split"), it is what the shipped CLI enforces (`--validity` help text: "required
non-empty at tiers 1-3"), and T-358 was ordered to execute the ledger
faithfully. The question for the join: is a planner-judgment tier split a
legitimate way to narrow an operator DIRECTIVE, or does it need its own
recorded reinterpretation act naming what it restricts? The layer's own
doctrine (PR-006, PR-007) says a narrowing of a declared reach is a
corrective-restrictive reinterpretation and must be recorded as one; V1-10
row 28 narrowed a DIRECTIVE without publishing such a record.

OPEN-QUESTION: LEDGER-A -- T-358 AC-4 and V1-52 contradict each other, and
the records follow V1-52. AC-4: "EVERY RECORD CARRIES, without exception:
`sources` including the DOI token for the addendum ... authority_tier 1 with
`tier_evidence` naming the operator-directive anchor the synthesis fixed."
V1-52 rows 8 and 9 fix tier 3, row 8's tier_evidence at ["T-352"] with no DOI
token, and row 9's sources at [T-347, T-352, decision:T-339#SDR-17.8] with no
DOI token at all. Live: PR-012 is tier 3 with a DOI in sources but none in
tier_evidence; PR-013 is tier 3 with no DOI anywhere. The records are RIGHT --
the task description makes the ledger governing ("The record ledger, the
subject slugs, the tier evidence anchors, the operation types and the sources
tokens are all fixed by ... synthesis-v1-requirements.md; your job is to
execute it faithfully"), V1-52's tier reasoning explains both tier-3 rows,
and row 9's authority genuinely is T-347's verdicted finding rather than the
addendum. The DISCLOSURE is what is short: worker-v1-6 disclosed only the
narrow row-8 tier_evidence asymmetry and did not flag that row 9 carries no
DOI at all or that two rows contradict AC-4's "authority_tier 1 ... without
exception". Recorded, not charged: AC-4's over-broad wording is the defect,
and the join should reconcile the acceptance criterion to the ledger rather
than the ledger to the criterion.

=== EXAMINED AND CLEARED (recorded so nobody re-litigates) ===

DECISION: cleared -- PR-006's "Author-declared ratios bind at publication as
the primary reference" reads wider than section 3's "This narrows the
interpretive range and is the primary reference", and reads at first glance
as contradicting SDR-02's confirmation gate, since every one of the nine
prints "scope: UNCONFIRMED (does not bind)". It does not. PRECEDENT.md's own
confirmation doctrine separates the two: "Rejecting a scope claim does not
reject the ratio underneath it: the ratio remains binding at tier; the
record's reach becomes undefined and is treated as persuasive-only." The
unconfirmed state suspends the SCOPE claim, never the ratio. Consistent.

DECISION: cleared -- INTERPRETIVE-CODE-A. PR-008 says the code is "amendable
only through the overruling-grade protocol, at tier 1 or 2"; A3's parenthetical
says "(tier-2 path)". Not an unauthorised widening: INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md's own
IC-13, shipped by T-356 and already verdicted, reads "amendable only through
the overruling-grade protocol -- a published registry record, at tier 1 or
tier 2", so the record enacts the constitutional artifact verbatim, and tier 1
is HIGHER authority than tier 2 on the same ladder, so admitting it widens who
may amend upward only. The record also adds the clause A3 implies and IC-13
states outright ("an ordinary edit to the document without a published
amending record is invalid").
